newsitem.title: EGYPT: Egypt says Israeli aspirations are "nonsense".
newsitem.headline: Egypt says Israeli aspirations are "nonsense".

text.p: Egypt thinks Israel's expectations from Middle East peace talks are "nonsense", plausible only to the ignorant or the mad, Foreign Minister Amr Moussa said in an interview published on Tuesday.

Moussa told the London-based Arabic newspaper Asharq al-Awsat the new Israeli government wanted to impose what he called an Israeli peace, rather than a balanced peace in which it makes compromises with its Arab neighbours.

"Israel wants security without there being a Palestinian state or even effective autonomy, without complete withdrawal from the Golan or complete withdrawal from Lebanon. And then it wants peace? Obviously nonsense," he added.
"Anyone who believes in such a possibility is either ignorant or mad," he said.

But he denied that rightwing Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu fitted this description. "So he must reconsider this policy of his so that he doesn't move everything to a very grave situation," he added.
He said that since taking office in June Netanyahu had only worsened the situation but he still had a chance to change.

"He knows these dangers but the greatest danger would be if he became dogmatic and ideological. If it turns out that the belief in expansion and a greater Israel still survives, that means we are back at square one and I honestly hope that this impression is not correct," he added.

Moussa said he had no magic recipe for persuading Netanyahu to make progress towards peace but the first step should be that the Arabs stand together and reject Netanyahu's approach. "If that happens, the situation will definitely change," he said.
